messages:
Avery Johnson: Quick field feedback from a call today — prospect really cared about tool calling + structured outputs. Our current live demo example ("calendar" tool) felt a bit toy-ish. They asked if we have something more compelling + production-y to show live (ideally w/ JSON schema output). Any ideas we can standardize?

Markus Klein: Yep, we’ve been hearing that. Calendar is easy but doesn’t land for infra/platform folks. Suggest a “support agent” flow with:
- structured output (ticket fields)
- a retrieval tool (kb_search)
- optional escalation tool (create_jira)
All synthetic data, but it feels real.

Renee Sullivan: +1. We can do a scripted scenario:
1) user: “I was double-charged — what do I do?”
2) model calls `kb_search(query)`
3) model returns structured JSON: `{category, priority, refund_eligibility, next_steps, citations[]}`
4) model calls `create_ticket(payload)`
Then show the Console trace with tool spans.

Monica Patel: From SDK side we can make it crisp. If we keep it to 2 tools max it stays reliable.
We can also show strict JSON schema / structured output enforcement (reject + retry) so it’s not “best effort JSON”. That’s usually the ‘oh wow’ moment.

Alex Martinez: We already have most of this in the demo app repo, just not wired as the default scenario.
I can add a “run scenario: support_triage” command that:
- streams assistant tokens
- shows tool call args in the terminal (sanitized)
- validates against a schema and demonstrates a retry on failure (only once, so it doesn’t drag)

Soojin Lee: Messaging angle that worked in another demo: “This is how you keep LLM output deterministic enough to hand to downstream systems.”
If we tie it to production risk (“no malformed payloads in your ticketing / refunds pipeline”) it lands better than “look, it can call tools”.

Simran Kaur: For enterprise folks, add a quick line: tools can be customer-owned endpoints (in their VPC) + audit logs show exactly what was called. Even if we don’t live-demo the private network part, we can narrate it.

Avery Johnson: Love the support triage idea. They literally asked “can you show me a payload I’d be comfortable sending to an API?” So schema validation + retry is perfect.
Do we have example JSON schema we can show without it turning into a wall of text?

Monica Patel: Yep. Keep it small: 6–8 fields, one nested array.
Also: we can show a “bad output” once (missing required field), then the retry succeeds. That demonstrates guardrails without being a long tangent.

Markus Klein: Action items?
- Renee: update talk track + run-of-show step for this module (5 mins max)
- Alex/Monica: implement/pin scenario in the demo app + confirm stable output
- Soojin: 1 slide / speaker note: “structured output = deterministic integration”
I’ll also ask Design for 2 backup screenshots in case live tool call flakes.

Renee Sullivan: I’ll draft the script + expected outputs (synthetic) and share in the enablement folder. Also adding an objection path: “What if tool is down?” → show fallback / graceful degradation story.

Alex Martinez: I’ll take the demo app changes. Will pin SDK versions and add a one-liner in the README: “do not upgrade day-of-demo.”

Avery Johnson: Perfect. If we can ship this before next week, I’ll use it in my exec demo. :thumbsup:

Markus Klein: Timeline: aiming to have a dry-run by Thu. I’ll post here when it’s ready + link the exact command + expected terminal output so it’s repeatable.
